title: Workflow
description: A workflow of a mode: steps of four kinds, run one after another and saved after each.

trigger.description: What starts the workflow: an event, a schedule, or only a person.

event.description: The name of the event that starts it.

budget.description: Limits for a run of the workflow.

name.description: Kebab-case, starting with a letter; not constructor, a name every JavaScript object has.

budget.description: Limits for a run; every nested call draws from the same budget.

items.description: The most items the run may handle.

usd.description: The most US dollars the run may spend.

tokens.description: The most model tokens the run may use.

minutes.description: The most minutes the run may take.

choice.description: One named answer of an approval. Without a rule it is always offered.

does.description: What taking the choice does, in one sentence the owner reads beside its name on the card.

when.description: The rule: an earlier step's output, $steps.<id>.output with an optional path, that is true or false. When it is false the choice is withheld, and what the step shows gives the reason under withheld.<choice>. A rule that is neither fails the step.

step.description: One step: an action, an approval, a wait or a foreach.

action.description: An action of this mode, or interface.action of an interface it requires.

input.description: Values are literals or references; without it, the output of the step before.

id.description: The step's id, unique in the whole file; its output is saved under it.

approval.description: The question put to the owner about what the step shows.

show.description: What the owner approves; without it, the output of the step before.

choices.description: The named answers the owner may give, in order; without it, the owner approves or rejects. The choice taken is the step's output as choice, beside what it showed as content.

quotes.description: The ids of earlier action steps whose skills a card's judged lines may cite, or of steps an earlier foreach runs in each item; a line cites such a step with its item, counted from 0, as source.item.

id.description: The step's id, unique in the whole file; its output is saved under it.

wait.description: How long to wait, as a whole number of minutes, hours or days: 30m, 2h, 3d.

id.description: The step's id, unique in the whole file; its output is saved under it.

foreach.description: A reference that resolves to a list; the steps run once per element, in order unless sideBySide is given.

sideBySide.description: How many elements may run at the same time, from 2 to 8: a whole number, or a reference resolved and checked each time the foreach starts or resumes. The output stays in the order of the list. When an element fails, the others still run to their end, then the run waits for the owner with every failure named; resume --rerun runs the failed ones again.

oneOf.description: A reference to a whole number from 2 to 8: $settings.<key>, $steps.<id>.output with an optional path, $trigger, or $item of an enclosing foreach.

itemName.description: How a card names an item of this foreach where a line cites a step in it: id and title are each $item or $item.<path>, read by the kernel from the item the foreach recorded. The card says for <id> (<title>), each made one line and cut, the id to 40 characters and the title to 80; without itemName, or when the id reads no text, it names the item by its place, such as the 1st of 3 items of step <foreach>.

id.description: The step's id, unique in the whole file; its output is saved under it.

steps.description: The steps run for each item, in order.
